question: On reducing the marked price of his goods by ₹28, a shopkeeper gains 20%. If the cost price of the article be ₹560 and it is sold at the marked price, what will be the gain per cent?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial profit = 20% of CP = 20% of ₹560 = ₹112.

If no discount is given, the selling price equals the marked price.

New profit = Initial profit + Discount given = 112 + 28 = ₹140.

New Gain % = (New Profit ÷ CP) × 100% = (140 ÷ 560) × 100% = 25%.

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) = ₹560

Discount = ₹28

Gain % after discount = 20%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = CP × (100 + Gain%) ÷ 100

Marked Price (MP) = SP + Discount

Gain % = [(New SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100
